### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints), invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, a path literal in a comment in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints), /forms/:slug (route, a path literal in a comment in registerFormEndpoints))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_option (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints), /forms/:slug (route, a path literal in a comment in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, a path literal in a comment in registerFormEndpoints))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in registerFormEndpoints), /forms/:slug (route, a path literal in a comment in registerFormEndpoints))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fef543bd93891fb4656ec433d7a4b6d85c5f10db` — the merge of head `4245716d349c26b21542e5f3bc3b12502f38784b` into base `ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fef543bd93891fb4656ec433d7a4b6d85c5f10db && git checkout fef543bd93891fb4656ec433d7a4b6d85c5f10db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21 4245716d349c26b21542e5f3bc3b12502f38784b && git checkout -B drift-repro ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21 && git merge --no-ff 4245716d349c26b21542e5f3bc3b12502f38784b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ca64f6f9ea9e23a1c444d01faa09ea648aa32b21` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4e67f5a7dff8fff7c4717f352130fe1496865921`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/public-form-option-subset.test.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (FormFieldSchema `options`, FormSelectOptionSchema), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (SelectOptionSchema), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (FieldErrorCode), packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts (the engine's `invalid_option` producer, `optionValues`, `buildFieldError`), packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.ts, packages/types/src/validation-failure.ts, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, ui/apps/console/src/components/FormPage.tsx (consumer), HotCRM src/service/views/case.view.ts and src/service/objects/case.object.ts (consumer). Prose faces read for ② and non-contradiction only: .changeset/27606-public-form-option-subset.md, content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Net diff against `main` at this head: 4 files, +353/-9; the two non-prose paths are the floor and both are read whole. Inputs: card #27606 body and all three comments (triage 6500544109, the claim 6509299862, the dev report 6510493301 read as a claim to verify), PR #27766 body, file list and diff, the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set change (the narrowing).** `POST /forms/:slug/submit` now refuses, before `createData`, a non-empty value in a declared field whose form entries list `options`, when the value (or any element of an array value) is not among the union of those entries' `value`s. Everything else the door accepted it still accepts. Right: this is the one narrowing the card asks for, and nothing is widened (`allowedFields`, `requiredFields`, the file judgement and the `201` answer are untouched; `fileValued` is renamed `valued` and reused, same predicate).
- **`invalid_option` is an existing ledgered code, not a new one.** `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` lists it in the closed `FieldErrorCode` enum ("not a member of the field's declared options"); `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx` lists it under "Closed sets and references"; the engine answers it on this same route for a value outside the object's options (`record-validator.ts`, the single select arm and the multi-value arm, with the `invalid_option` / `invalid_option_value` message keys the door now reuses). The deviation from the order's `invalid_value` is right: `invalid_value` is the catalog's "a reason no other member names", and a non-member of a declared option list is exactly what `invalid_option` names. No new public error code, no new message key (`invalid_option` and `invalid_option_value` exist in all four locales of `BUILTIN_VALIDATION_MESSAGES`), so `Clause-②` stays `no (narrowing)`.
- **One refusal envelope.** The new entries are pushed into the same `refused` array the `required` and file judgements fill and thrown through the same `validationFailure(...)`, which `mapDataError` already maps to the flat `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[]`; the local `code` union widens to admit `'invalid_option'` and an optional `constraint`, both keys `FieldErrorSchema` declares. No second envelope, no exported type changes (`registerFormEndpoints` and `FormRouteHost` signatures unchanged). Right.
- **Multi-select values.** `Array.isArray(value) ? value : [value]`, judged element by element with `String(v)` against `String(o.value)`, the first outside element named through `invalid_option_value`: the engine's own reading (`optionValues` stringifies the same way). A scalar sent to a multi-valued field is judged as a one-element list, which is what `normalizeMultiValueFields` would have made of it downstream. Right.
- **Empty optional values.** `valued` already drops `isMissing` values (absent, null, blank string); the loop re-applies `isEmptyForRequired(def, value)` so `[]` on a declared multi-valued field is not judged either. Same emptiness rule as `required`. Right.
- **Fields without a row subset.** A bare-string entry, or an object entry with no `options` (or `options: []`), writes `null` for the field and `null` is sticky: once any entry offers the full set the field is not narrowed, whatever another entry lists; both orderings of the two entries land on `null`. A field no entry narrows falls through to the engine as before. Right, and the `WIDE_FORM` test pins the two-entry case.
- **Label vs value.** The door compares stored values only. The spec's `FormSelectOptionSchema` is `SelectOptionSchema` minus `default`/`kind`: a strict object with `label` required and `value` a lowercase `SystemIdentifierSchema`, so a parsed row cannot carry a label-only or bare-string option; `translateMetadataDocument('view', ...)` rewrites option labels keyed by `opt.value` and never the value. The console posts values. Right.
- **Hidden / conditionally visible entries.** The subset is collected off every entry, including `hidden: true` and `visibleWhen` ones, where `required` is collected only off unconditional ones. The asymmetry is in the permissive direction (a hidden entry's `options` can only ADD offered values to the union or, listing none, un-narrow the field), and a value outside every subset the form lists was never offered to anyone. Acceptable; the PR body states it.
- **Test file.** Through the real route (RestServer, protocol, ObjectQL, sqlite in memory; only `getMetaItems` stubbed), it pins the four refusal classes (outside the subset, outside the object, multi-valued element, one envelope with `required`), the stored control, the four emptiness controls and the two boundaries, and asserts `createData` is never called and no row is stored on a refusal. `installDefaultOrganization` exists at `packages/rest/src/default-organization.testkit.ts`; `packages/rest` `typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit && pnpm check:test-typecheck`. Shape is right; its 11/11 reading is the dev's claim, carried by the head's `Test Core` shards (in progress at this read).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `'@objectstack/rest': patch`. Right by the rule: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no metadata key, value or type changes; a REST door enforces a key the form entry already declares and `GET /forms/:slug` already serves), so the level is `patch` with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition kept. Both line-initial declarations are present and match the PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- `**BREAKING**` banner present, with Before / Now / Unchanged / Who sees it / The remedy.
- ADR-0087 disposition: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a member of the gate's `CATEGORIES`. The body carries no FROM/TO rewrite, no migration heading and no two-column rewrite table ("The remedy" says what value to send, not how to rewrite a source), so the category's one mechanical refusal does not fire; `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are both `success` on this head. The honest category: no schema key moves, no export changes, nothing for `migrate meta` to rewrite.
- Docs sentence (`content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx` section 2) states the code's behaviour: refused with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the field, `invalid_option`, the subset's values only; an entry listing none offers the full set. No contradiction with the tree. The Docs Drift Check's other eight named docs cite the `invalid_option` / `invalid_value` literals in general; the catalog page already lists `invalid_option`, so none contradicts the change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1, `invalid_option` instead of `invalid_value`: answered in ①, right.
- Dev deviation 2, eslint on the two changed files only: `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head, so the repo-wide run is carried.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally: `Lint & Repo Gates` `success` carries it.
- "An entry's `options: []` is read as listing no subset": judged right. The row face is `z.array(FormSelectOptionSchema).optional()`; the FIELD face refuses an empty list at parse, the row face does not, and the renderer derives options from the object field when a row lists none, so "no subset" is the consistent reading.
- "A hidden or conditionally visible entry is still judged": judged acceptable, see ①.
- "The console's public form page still offers every option until the domain:ui half": true on `main` (`FormPage.tsx` `buildSections` sets `options: normalizeOptions(def.options)` off the OBJECT field and never reads the entry's `options`). Until that half lands, a visitor who picks an excluded value on such a form sees the 400 naming the field and the allowed values instead of storing a value the form never offered. Triage 6500544109 routed the renderer half to its own `domain:ui` card; this record does not verify that card exists, and that is the one open dependency to escalate: the domain:ui seat's card for `FormPage.tsx` reading the entry's `options` (blocked by #27496 per triage).
- `open_questions: []`; `out_of_scope_findings`: the renderer half, noted as above. No flag left unanswered.
- Check-runs on `4e67f5a7` as read: every completed, non-skipped run is `success` (Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, all `Lint ·` legs, `Type Check · consumer / debt ledger / source gates`, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness). Still `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/8 to 8/8)` and `Type Check · workspace`. No failure read. The verdict below is the review's; the gate verdicts are theirs.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: `FormFieldSchema.options` is described as letting a row "offer a deliberate subset" of the field's members, `GET /forms/:slug` serves the row's entries whole (`safeForm` filters entries by field type only), and the engine judges a write against the OBJECT's options alone. The door therefore accepted what the spec declared withheld. This change makes the spec's own refusal real at the only anonymous write door; it takes no declared capability away from any consumer, because no spec surface ever declared that a value outside a row's `options` could be stored through the form.

Attempts to break it, each read in the cited code:

- **Label-vs-value shapes.** Strict row-option shape (`label` + lowercase `value`), so a parsed row has values; the door reads `value` only. Holds.
- **A row subset naming a value the field lacks.** The door admits it (it is in the subset); the engine then refuses it with the same `invalid_option` code in the same envelope, naming the object's options. Nothing is stored that the object does not allow. Holds; the door's `allowed` would name a value the object lacks, which is the author's mistake surfaced, not a hole.
- **Picklist-bound and dependent fields.** A field with `picklist:` still goes through the engine's picklist arm after the door; a row's `dependsOn` is a client-side cascade the door never evaluated before either, and the row's declared `options` list is the ceiling the renderer cascades inside. No record-type option sets exist in `packages/spec` to judge. Holds.
- **The console's public form page.** Renders the object's full option list today; an excluded value now answers a 400 naming the field and the allowed values. A UX regression only for a form that declares a row subset, and on `main`'s own corpus no shipped public form does: `examples/app-crm` and `examples/app-showcase` contact-us forms declare no row `options`, nor does HotCRM's `web_to_lead`. Holds, with the renderer card as the follow-through.
- **HotCRM's web-to-case form.** `web_to_case` carries no `priority` row at all (the maintainer's fallback for exactly this defect, with `case_sla_defaults` capping a guest's `critical` at `high`), so the door's allow-list drops a posted `priority` before this judgement runs. Unaffected today; the fix is what lets HotCRM put `{ field: 'priority', options: [low, medium, high] }` back once the renderer reads it. Holds.
- **Fail direction on malformed data.** See should-fix 1: a row whose option entries carry no `value` fails closed (refuses everything on that field), never open.

Findings:

- **should-fix 1** (form-routes.ts, the `optionSubsets` collection): an entry whose `options` are non-empty but carry no `value` (bare strings, or objects without `value`) yields an EMPTY `Set`, which is truthy, so `if (!subset) continue;` does not skip it and every non-empty value is refused with `allowed` empty. The engine's `optionValues` and the console's `normalizeOptions` both read a bare-string option as its own value. Unreachable through a parsed view (the strict `FormSelectOptionSchema` refuses that shape; every stored-row seam replays the conversion chain before the strict parse), so not a must-fix; read a string entry as its value, or treat a subset that collected no values as `null`.
- **should-fix 2** (form-routes.ts, the `refused.push` for the subset): the engine's `invalid_option` refusal (`buildFieldError`) ships the offending element as `value` beside `constraint.allowed`; the door's entry ships `constraint.allowed` only and names the element in `message` alone. Two producers of one code on one route should ship the same keys; add `value: String(elements[outside])` on the multi-valued branch (and the scalar on the single branch), as `FieldErrorSchema.value` declares.

No must-fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1Np3hU7RQnA13YZcL`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4245716d349c26b21542e5f3bc3b12502f38784b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/public-form-option-subset.test.ts (the delta 4e67f5a7..4245716d, one commit, +48/-5, these two paths only; the prose faces are byte-identical to the head reviewed in comment 6510723571) + packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts (`optionValues`, `buildFieldError`, the single and multi-value `invalid_option` arms), packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts (FormSelectOptionSchema), packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts (FieldErrorSchema `value`).

Delta review on top of the PASS record for `4e67f5a7` (comment 6510723571): that record's ①–④ stand for everything the delta does not touch; this record judges the delta and re-reads the head's check-runs. The PR's file list is unchanged (4 files); the net diff against `main` is now +396/-9.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Should-fix 1 applied (bare-string option, empty subset).** In the `optionSubsets` collection, each offered option is read as `typeof o === 'string' ? o : o?.value`, added when neither `undefined` nor `null`; this is the engine's `optionValues` reading (`String(o)` for a non-object, `String(o.value)` for an object) and the console's `normalizeOptions`. The refusal loop now skips `!subset || subset.size === 0`, so a subset that collected no values narrows nothing and the field falls through to the engine's own judgement. Accept-set effect against `4e67f5a7`: a row whose options carry no readable value no longer refuses every value (that head failed closed on malformed data); a row with bare-string options now narrows to those strings instead of refusing everything. Both are inside the one narrowing already declared; neither widens past what `main` accepts (the engine still judges every value against the object). Right.
- **Should-fix 2 applied (`value` on the wire).** The multi-valued arm ships `value: String(elements[outside])`, the offending element, beside `constraint.allowed`; the single arm ships none. That is exactly the engine's shape: its multi-value `fail(...)` passes `String(v)` as `value`, its single-select `fail(...)` passes `undefined`. The local `refused` element type gains `value?: string`; `FieldErrorSchema.value` is declared `z.unknown().optional()`. Same envelope, same `validationFailure`, no exported surface moved. Right.
- **Nothing else moved.** The union/`null` logic for multiple entries, the emptiness rule, the `required` and file judgements, the `invalid_option` / `invalid_option_value` catalog keys, `createData` and the `201` answer are untouched by the delta.
- **Tests.** `LOOSE_FORM` (served through the stubbed `getMetaItems`, the only way an unparsed shape reaches the door) pins: bare-string options narrow to their values (`critical` refused with `allowed: 'low, medium'`, `medium` stored); value-less options narrow nothing (`channel: 'phone'` stored); the single-arm refusal has no `value` key; the multi-arm refusal ships `value: 'security'` and `constraint.allowed: 'billing, outage'`. `expectRefused` gained a `slug` parameter; the earlier 11 cases are unchanged. 13 cases now; their green reading is the dev's claim, carried by the head's `Test Core` shards.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged by the delta: the changeset and the docs sentence are byte-identical to `4e67f5a7` (`@objectstack/rest: patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, BREAKING banner, one `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker). The delta ships no new key and no new code, and the changeset's "Unchanged" paragraph ("an entry that lists no `options` keeps the object's full set") is not contradicted by a value-less list also keeping it. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The two should-fixes of record 6510723571: both answered by the delta, as judged in ①. No new dev flag; no `open_questions`.
- The renderer-half escalation (the `domain:ui` card for `FormPage.tsx` reading the entry's `options`) stands as recorded on `4e67f5a7`; the delta does not bear on it.
- Check-runs on `4245716d` as read: completed, non-skipped, all `success` — Auto Label, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Test UI, filter. Still `in_progress`: Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, every other `Lint ·` leg (CI release and engine gates, ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, two scoped legs), Live E2E UI, Plan Test Core shards, and all four `Type Check ·` legs. No failure read. The gate verdicts are theirs; this verdict is the review's.

### ④ Design judgment

The delta moves the door's fail direction on a malformed row from closed (refuse every value) to the engine's judgement, and makes the two producers of `invalid_option` on this route ship the same keys. Attempts to break it: a row mixing one value-less entry with one valued entry for the same field unions to the valued set (the empty collection adds nothing and is not `null`), so the field is narrowed to what was readable, which is what the form publishes; a `null` option value is skipped rather than stringified to `"null"`, stricter than the engine's `String(o.value)` and in the safe direction; a bare-string option that names a value the object lacks is admitted by the door and refused by the engine as before. The console and HotCRM readings on `4e67f5a7` are unaffected (neither declares a row subset today). Holds.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
